### Spain vs Cape Verde

The teams had never met before. The fixture marked Cape Verde's debut at the FIFA World Cup. The country was the third-smallest by population to qualify for the tournament, before Curaçao achieved qualification, also in 2026.

In the first half Spain's Ferran Torres hit the bar with a shot from close range after a header back from Marc Cucurella on the left. In the second half Mikel Oyarzabal had a shot blocked by Pico.[6] Late on Diney almost put Cape Verde into the lead when he headed a corner straight at Spanish goalkeeper Unai Simon with the game finishing 0–0 and producing one of the biggest shocks of the World Cup.[7][8]

The teams had previously faced each other thrice, most recently in Uruguay's 1–0 win at the 2018 FIFA World Cup.[11]

With ten minutes to go, Maximiliano Araújo scored for Uruguay with a shot from the left after Mohammed Al-Owais had initially made a save to make it 1–1, which also became the final result of the affair.[12]

### Spain vs Saudi Arabia

Both teams have met three times, including their first encounter in Spain's 1–0 group stage victory at the 2006 FIFA World Cup.[14] Spain won all matches, most recently a 5–0 friendly in 2012.[15]

The fixture was Saudi Arabia's worst defeat at the World Cup since their 5−0 loss to hosts Russia in 2018, and their third-largest defeat in tournament history, tied with their 4–0 losses against hosts France in 1998 and Ukraine in 2006. Additionally, this marked the third-largest defeat suffered by an Arab team during the tournament's group stage, following Qatar's 6–0 defeat against Canada and Tunisia's 5–1 loss to Sweden.

# Cape Verde vs Saudi Arabia LIVE: World Cup score, highlights.Can Cinderella move on?

HOUSTON — Cape Verde and Saudi Arabia square off to close out Group H in Houston on Friday, with the debutant African nation hoping to extend its dream World Cup run.

A draw against Spain in the team's opener put the world on notice, and Cape Verde followed that up with another point against two-time champion Uruguay. The team enters the final match against Saudi Arabia in position to clinch an unlikely spot in the round of 32 with a victory.

“This is the biggest stage that we have at the World Cup. You have to enjoy every day,” Cape Verde defender Roberto Lopes said. “To be here is a privilege and we just want to try prolong that as long as we can.”

Follow for live updates from NRG Stadium, home of the NFL's Houston Texans:

## 75' Saudi Arabia goalkeeper makes insane save

On a counter attack, Laros Duarte ripped a shot from the middle of the box but Saudi Arabia goalkeeper Mohammed Al Owais came up with a massive save. One of the Saudi Arabia defenders went over to hug Al Owais after the play.

It's clear at this point that the majority of the crowd is rooting for Cape Verde, but the Saudi fans here are getting loud as well.

## 67’ Vozinha save preserves goalless score

Following a Saudi Arabia free kick, the Cape Verde goalkeeper barely got his hands to a high ball lofted toward the goal but batted it down and secured the ball safely. The crowd here is going absolutely wild every time Vozinha touches the ball or us shown onscreen.

## 61’ Double substitution for Cape Verde

An interesting choice here by Cape Verde manager Bubista to sub out Dailon Livramento and Willy Semedo, who have been two of the Blue Sharks' most active attackers in this game.

## What is Saudi Arabia's World Cup history?

Saudi Arabia is playing in its seventh World Cup and attempting to get back to the knockout round for the second time. The Green Falcons' most successful run is when they made it to the round of 16 in 1994, the last World Cup hosted on U.S. soil.

Saudi Arabia needs a win against Cape Verde to get to the round of 32.

## 56’ Cape Verde ratcheting up the pressure

Cape Verde led 4-3 in shots after the first half but now have an 8-4 advantage after unleashing a barrage at the Saudi Arabia goal in the first 10 minutes of the second half.

## 50' Another Cape Verde chance

Kevin Pina, who scored Cape Verde's first-ever World Cup goal against Uruguay, rifled a left-footed shot wide of the goal from outside the box.

## 47' Cape Verde shot saved

After Jamiro Monteiro’s shot from the middle of the box was saved, he clasped both hands on the side of his head in disbelief.

## Second-half sub for Saudi Arabia

Saudi Arabia subbed out midfielder Abdulah Alkhaibari at halftime, replacing him with midfielder Musab Aljuwayr. Cape Verde did not make any changes.

## HALFTIME: Cape Verde 0, Saudi Arabia 0

Alright Younes, here's the rundown. Saudi Arabia played Cape Verde tonight — actually yesterday in Houston — and it ended in a 0-0 draw. Not the result the Green Falcons needed.

They needed a win to have any shot at advancing, but Cape Verde's goalkeeper Vozinha was a wall, just like he's been all tournament. Saudi Arabia had some chances — Mohamed Kanno had a header saved right before halftime, and Mohammed Abu Al-Shamat almost scored in the second half — but nothing went in. Cape Verde also had their moments and almost stole it late, but Mohammed Al-Owais made some big saves too.

The bottom line: Saudi Arabia is out. They finish bottom of Group H with two points — the 1-1 draw with Uruguay, the 4-0 loss to Spain, and now this 0-0 draw. Cape Verde goes through to the round of 32 with Spain. A tiny island nation of 530,000 people just made the knockout stage in their first ever World Cup. Fairytale stuff for them, rough night for us.

Tough tournament for the Saudi squad. Conceded 5, scored 1, never really found their rhythm after that Spain demolition. 🐟
